result:
I’d make it safe to change your mind.

Not safe from consequences—if you’ve harmed someone, that still matters. Safe from the shame and social exile that make admitting error feel like losing yourself.

So many bad things persist because people must defend what they believe to protect who they are. If revising your views were seen as courage rather than weakness or betrayal, I think politics, science, families—even apologies—would work differently.

A world that can honestly say “I was wrong” is a world that can still become better.
